channel.title: AI Campaign News (AICN)
channel.description: A tracker of AI use in political campaigns, elections, and advocacy.

item.title: Meet Haystack: Social Listening Built for Democrats
item.description: Higher Ground Labs has announced Haystack, an AI-native social listening platform designed for Democratic communicators to monitor what voters are seeing and saying on social media.

item.title: Democrats are betting GOP's AI ads on Talarico and others will backfire
item.description: The Washington Post reports that Democratic campaigns are deliberately avoiding AI-generated video ads, betting that Republican use of such ads — including against candidates like Brian Talarico in Texas — will generate a backlash among voters skeptical of AI content.

item.title: Scoop: Washington Democrats allege AI misuse in GOP-backed mailer
item.description: Washington state Democrats allege that a GOP-backed mailer supporting candidate Michael Shepard misused AI, potentially in violation of Washington election law, according to Axios Seattle.

item.title: Congressman faces ethics complaint over AI generated graphic of opponent
item.description: A U.S. congressman is facing an ethics complaint after circulating an AI-generated graphic depicting an opponent, according to a local news report.

item.title: AI is reshaping high-stakes elections around the world
item.description: Semafor reports that partisan actors in Brazil, Israel, and the U.S. are gaming AI platforms to surface misleading information ahead of high-stakes elections, describing a cross-border pattern of AI-answer manipulation tied to active campaigns.

item.title: Exclusive: Democratic AI PAC takes its fight to Senate Republicans
item.description: Tomorrow Together, a Democratic PAC advocating for AI regulation, is spending $2.5 million on ads targeting Republican Senators Jon Husted in Ohio and Roger Marshall in Kansas, expanding its campaign beyond House races into competitive Senate contests.

item.title: UK Politicians Are Testing Their Messages on AI-Generated Focus Groups
item.description: UK politicians are using AI-generated focus groups — synthetic respondents — to pre-test campaign messaging before deploying it to real audiences, according to Bloomberg reporting.

item.title: The next election influence campaign will target your AI chatbot
item.description: Israeli threat intelligence firm VisionHeight has identified a coordinated network of at least 460 pages across 37 websites in 14 states — including Arizona, Georgia, Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin — publishing AI-optimized content designed to steer chatbot responses toward specific candidates in House races, Secretary of State contests, and local offices. The sites, with names like "Wolverine State Report" and "Peach State Bulletin," were configured to allow major AI crawlers to scrape them, and at least one — Tarheel State Report — was cited as a primary source by Perplexity; VisionHeight does not attribute the operation to a specific actor.

item.title: AI is changing what political campaigns say, and who gets to hear it
item.description: An AP report, syndicated from Minneapolis, examines how political campaigns are using AI to tailor messaging at the individual voter level — analyzing consumer data such as vehicle ownership, shopping habits, and homeownership to personalize outreach at scale in ways previously unavailable to most campaigns.

item.title: Voters Are Already Getting AI Answers About Your Campaign. They Just Don't Know It.
item.description: A new AAPC Foundation national survey of likely voters, discussed by Tarrance Group pollster B.J. Martino, finds that voters are already encountering AI-generated answers about campaigns through ambient AI tool use — often without knowing it — and that significant voter distrust and hard limits around campaign AI use are emerging from the data.

item.title: U . S . candidates have gone from spending nearly zero to $137 million on AI ads in one election cycle
item.description: Fortune reports that U.S. political advertisers went from near-zero to $137 million in AI-generated ad spending in a single election cycle, and adds a new detail not previously highlighted: more than 70% of AI campaign videos carried no disclaimer or disclosure that AI was used in their production.

item.title: Oregon outlet retracts story calling viral video of local candidate a deepfake
item.description: OregonLive reports that an Oregon outlet retracted its story labeling a viral video of Washington County candidate Nafisa Fai a deepfake after the evidence supporting that characterization fell apart, with Oregon Democrats having already publicly condemned the video.

item.title: Candidates campaign for AI attention
item.description: Marketplace reports on candidates actively shaping how their campaigns appear in AI-generated answers, treating AI search and answer tools as a new channel that campaigns need to optimize for alongside traditional digital outreach.

item.title: Is AI Reshaping the 2026 Midterms? $137 Million Spent on AI-Generated Political Ads
item.description: IBTimes reports that Republican-affiliated groups account for 88% of the $137 million spent on AI-generated political ads in the 2026 midterms, adding a partisan breakdown to the Wesleyan Media Project figures already in circulation.

item.title: AI Makes Everything Look the Same. Here’s How True Experts Stand Out
item.description: A Campaigns & Elections op-ed argues that campaigns and consultants over-relying on AI for creative and strategic work risk blending into a homogenized middle, and that differentiation requires human expertise layered on top of AI output.

item.title: How AI is changing political campaigns and voter targeting in Minnesota
item.description: The Star Tribune reports on how Minnesota political campaigns are deploying AI for voter targeting and other campaign functions in the 2026 midterm cycle, examining specific adoption patterns in a competitive battleground state.

item.title: Political Advertisers Have Spent At Least $137 Million on AI-Generated Ads
item.description: The Wesleyan Media Project identified 220 political ads produced at least in part with AI tools in 2026, with combined advertiser spending of at least $137 million — a substantially higher figure than the $80 million tallied by earlier tracking efforts.

item.title: Small Dollars, Big Problems
item.description: A Campaign Trend newsletter reports on how political chatbots are being built or used in ways that expose where voters live, alongside coverage of TikTok's paid content featuring state Rep. James Talarico.

item.title: Tech: Key AI group added no Q3 donations
item.description: Leading the Future, an AI-industry-backed super PAC with ties to major tech figures, reported zero new donations in Q3 2026, according to new FEC disclosures.

item.title: Some Lessons from the Trenches: What I learned and thoughts on how to move forward
item.description: Cat Stern, who served as Paid Media Director on both the Biden and Harris 2024 presidential campaigns, outlines five operational lessons for Democratic campaigns: unify all paid media channels under one team, invest early in ground-game organizing, enforce tighter message discipline, limit pre-flight ad testing to high-stakes executions, and define clearer roles for outside consultants.

item.title: AI Political Field Guide: Terminology Decoder (September 2026 Edition)
item.description: Writer Kate Gage publishes an AI terminology decoder for fall 2026, mapping how key terms—including "superintelligence," "safety," "EA," and "pause"—have shifted meaning depending on which faction uses them, tracing conflicts among the Trump administration, the Tech Right (including David Sacks), AI Safety advocates, the Sanders-Casar bill camp, and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei following a September 2026 White House executive order and voluntary CEO accord.

item.title: Why Silicon Valley's AI super PACs aren't talking about AI
item.description: Fast Company examines Silicon Valley-backed AI super PACs that are spending in the 2026 midterms but are deliberately not making AI a campaign message, instead funding races on other issues while keeping AI policy goals in the background.

item.title: $16 million spent on AI-edited political ads in the 2026 midterm election season
item.description: A report puts AI-edited political ad spending in the 2026 midterm season at $16 million, adding a dollar figure to the volume of AI-assisted ad production in the current cycle.

item.title: How American Political Campaigns Are Using AI—and What They're Spending on the Tools
item.description: Bruce Schneier and Nathan E. Sanders, writing in The Guardian, analyzed FEC campaign finance disclosure data to identify which U.S. campaigns, parties, and committees are purchasing AI tools and how much they are spending, finding that AI is rapidly becoming an essential part of campaign operations.

item.title: Why one spoiler candidate is now trying to replicate his work nationwide
item.description: Aaron Day, a political operative known for recruiting spoiler candidates, is using AI to scale his third-party candidate recruitment and placement operation nationally ahead of the 2026 midterms, according to Semafor.

item.title: FullPAC Launches GOTV AI, the Campaign Strategy Platform Built on the Record of American Elections
item.description: FullPAC has launched GOTV AI, a campaign strategy platform it says is trained on the historical record of American elections and designed to support get-out-the-vote and campaign planning efforts.

item.title: The AI Election Ad Surge: Why the 2026 Midterms Need a Common Transparency Baseline
item.description: A Campaigns & Elections op-ed argues that campaigns in 2026 are producing far more ad versions across more screens at unprecedented speed thanks to AI, and calls for a common transparency baseline for AI-generated election ads given the current patchwork of state requirements.

item.title: We've tracked $80M of spending on almost 170 AI-generated political ads this year – it's weird
item.description: An ad-tracking effort has identified roughly 170 AI-generated political ads with approximately $80 million in combined spending in 2026, finding that many of these ads carry no AI disclosure due to inconsistent state-level requirements.

item.title: How AI is playing in the post-Nancy Pelosi race
item.description: In the California congressional race to succeed Nancy Pelosi, campaigns for state Sen. Scott Wiener and San Francisco Supervisor Connie Chan have both deployed paid ads explicitly invoking artificial intelligence, making AI a central message in the contest.

item.title: OpenAI wants to curb misleading election deepfakes
item.description: OpenAI is taking steps to make it harder for users to generate misleading election deepfakes through its platforms, implementing restrictions targeting bad actors seeking to interfere in U.S. elections.
